**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT), medium severity.**

**What the document says.** The only audit right binding us is Paragraph 9 (Keeping and Inspection of Books for Segment S and T):
- **9.8** — "Any Party shall have the right to review or audit the relevant books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs pursuant to this Paragraph 9," with the audited Party entitled to recover from the requesting Party "the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying with the review or audit."
- **9.9** — audit rights "shall only be exercisable through the F&ASC in accordance with the F&ASC's audit procedures."

**Assessment against the rule.**
| Term | Document | Position |
|---|---|---|
| Frequency | Unspecified — unlimited | Fails fallback (once/year) |
| Notice | None | Fails fallback (15 days) |
| Cost | Requesting Party pays 100% of compliance costs | Better than preferred |
| System access | None — books and records only | Meets preferred |

Cost allocation and scope are already favourable, but the complete absence of a frequency cap and any notice period is walk-away territory ("unlimited or unannounced audits"), not a minor sub-element. Paragraph 9.9's F&ASC channelling is procedural only and supplies neither a cap nor notice.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** A single minimal edit to 9.8 inserting "not more than once in any twelve (12) month period and on not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice" and "during normal business hours," leaving the favourable cost-recovery sentences untouched. Because the clause is mutual, these limits protect us and apply equally to our own review rights; the comment offers 15 days' notice as a fallback if that better suits the F&ASC's procedures.
